sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of high-level languages. Give two examples used for programming today.
questions.answer: High-level languages are close to English, easy to learn, write and correct, and machine-independent, so programs can run on different computers. Examples: C++, Java (also Python, BASIC).

or.q: What is application software? How is it classified?
or.answer: Application software is a set of programs written to do a specific task for the user. It is classified as generalised packages (e.g. Word, Excel, Oracle) and customised packages (made for one organisation, e.g. payroll, student management).

questions.q: What is the difference between a compiler and an assembler?
questions.answer: A compiler translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine language (object program). An assembler translates a program written in assembly language (mnemonics) into machine language.

or.q: What is a high-level language? Give at least two examples.
or.answer: A high-level language is close to English, easy to learn and machine-independent; it is translated into machine language by a compiler or interpreter. Examples: BASIC, FORTRAN, C, C++, Java.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the names of any three commonly used generalised packages.
questions.answer: Word processor (MS Word), spreadsheet (MS Excel), presentation (PowerPoint) — also DBMS such as MS Access or Oracle, graphics tools such as Paint Shop Pro.

or.q: Write the names of any three Database Management System (DBMS) programs.
or.answer: MS Access, Oracle, MS SQL Server (also MySQL, FoxPro).

questions.q: What is a data source? Write any two methods by which you can prepare a data source.
questions.answer: A data source is a file containing the variable information (names, addresses, etc.) arranged as records and fields, used in mail merge. Methods: (1) type a new list in the Mail Merge Wizard (New Address List); (2) create a table in a Word document; (3) use an Excel worksheet (or an Access table).

questions.q: Explain the role of the documents involved in Mail Merge in MS Word.
questions.answer: Main document — contains the text and graphics that stay the same in every copy, with merge fields where the changing data goes. Data source — a file (Word table, Excel sheet, Access table) holding the variable information such as names and addresses in rows (records) and columns (fields). Merge document — the result: one personalised copy for each record, which can be printed, saved or e-mailed.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Define organisational domain. What are its types? (b) Explain the Domain Name System with an example.
questions.answer:
(a) The organisational domain is the rightmost part of a domain name that shows the type of organisation: .ac (academic), .com (commercial), .edu (educational), .gov (government), .net (network resources), .org (non-profit). Geographic domains show the country: .in, .uk, .us, .au, .jp.
(b) Every computer on the Internet has a numeric IP address that is hard to remember. DNS (Domain Name System) gives each host a name and translates the name into its IP address. For example in www.nios.ac.in: www — World Wide Web, nios — host computer, ac — academic organisation, in — India.
